Output of `forgecycle help roadmap <command>` for ForgeCycle 0.6.1.

## forgecycle roadmap decompose

Assess a large plan and write ordered task files.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap decompose [options] <plan.md>

Assess a large plan and write ordered task files.

Arguments:
  <plan.md>        The plan, a Markdown file

Options:
  --policy NAME    Use routing policy NAME's decomposer candidates (default:
                   the configured default_policy)
  --decomposer ID  Use a candidate listed as Decomposer in the active policy
                   for this invocation only
  --output DIR     Write to DIR (default: a new tasks/<plan-name>-<suffix>
                   directory)
  -h, --help       Show this help

The Decomposer investigates the relevant code read-only and writes
repository-grounded task context and component-level guidance. The output
directory holds:
  - roadmap.md
  - roadmap.json, the machine-readable task order, files, prerequisites, and
    decisions
  - decisions.md, the decisions a human must make
  - source-plan.md
  - one <task-id>.md per task

decisions.md numbers the decisions Q01, Q02, …, each written for someone who
has not just read the code: its context with terms explained, what depends on
it, the tasks it affects, each option with its consequences, a recommended
answer with its reason, and empty Unclear: and Answer: lines. A question
missing one of these parts is rejected.

Review the roadmap and answer every decision before running it: roadmap run
refuses to start while one is open, and gives every task's Planner, Builder,
and Reviewer the answers. If a decision is unclear, write what you do not
understand after its Unclear: line and run roadmap questions. Each task's
Planner later re-investigates the selected base and writes the authoritative
file-level plan.

A warning names tasks with more acceptance criteria than
decompose.max_acceptance_criteria (default: 6).

See also: forgecycle help roadmap questions, forgecycle help roadmap run
```

## forgecycle roadmap questions

Rewrite unclear decisions and add the ones a roadmap misses.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap questions [options] <DIR|roadmap.json>

Rewrite unclear decisions and add the ones a roadmap misses.

Arguments:
  <DIR|roadmap.json>  The roadmap manifest 'roadmap decompose' wrote; DIR means
                      DIR/roadmap.json

Options:
  --policy NAME       Use routing policy NAME's decomposer candidates (default:
                      the configured default_policy)
  --decomposer ID     Use a candidate listed as Decomposer in the active policy
                      for this invocation only
  -h, --help          Show this help

The Decomposer reads, read-only, the roadmap, its task files, its source plan,
and its decisions document with the answers given so far. Every decision with
text after its Unclear: line is rewritten under its own ID to answer what you
asked, with your question quoted as You asked, and its Unclear: line is
cleared; an answer you wrote is kept. Decisions that a task's Planner or
Reviewer would otherwise stop the roadmap run to ask are appended as open
decisions, numbered after the highest Q ID. Nothing else changes.

Run it after answering or marking the decompose decisions, since answers can
raise new ones. Each candidate tried, and its one repair attempt, is a billed
model call.

The manifest must name a decisions document (exit 65 otherwise). A candidate
that changes the repository's Git state fails with exit 22.

See also: forgecycle help roadmap decompose
```

## forgecycle roadmap run

Run a roadmap's tasks in order, each on the previous one's head.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap run [options] <DIR|roadmap.json>

Run a roadmap's tasks in order, each on the previous one's head.

Arguments:
  <DIR|roadmap.json>  The roadmap manifest 'roadmap decompose' wrote; DIR means
                      DIR/roadmap.json

Options:
  --policy NAME       Use routing policy NAME for every task run (default: the
                      configured default_policy)
  --base REF          Start from Git revision REF, resolved once (default:
                      HEAD)
  --approval POLICY   Override every task's front matter: autonomous,
                      plan-and-final, every-turn, or custom
  --planner ID        Use candidate ID as Planner for the task runs this
                      invocation starts or resumes
  --builder ID        Use candidate ID as Builder for the task runs this
                      invocation starts or resumes; not a read-only candidate
  --reviewer ID       Use candidate ID as Reviewer for the task runs this
                      invocation starts or resumes
  --skip ID[,ID...]   Skip tasks whose outcome is already on the base; their
                      dependents still run
  --auto-resume       Pass --auto-resume to every task run
  --accept-defaults   Take the recommended answer for every unanswered
                      decision, in the snapshot only; the document is not
                      changed, and a decision marked unclear is never answered
  -h, --help          Show this help

Each task runs as an ordinary task run, with its own state, handoffs, branch,
worktree, and approval policy, started as a child 'forgecycle task run <task>
--base <integration head>' with inherited output. After a task run's done
verdict, the roadmap run fast-forwards its own branch
forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id> to that task run's head; it never touches
your branches. Its state is stored under
.forgecycle/roadmap-runs/<roadmap-run-id>/. --policy, --auto-resume, and
--approval (when given) are stored for later task runs.

Before anything is created, every task that is not skipped is checked: its
front matter must parse, its approval and checkpoints must be valid, and it
must not set forgecycle.base (exit 65 names the task).

Every decision in the manifest's decisions document must be answered and none
marked unclear. On a terminal, roadmap run shows each unanswered decision in
full and asks it: Enter takes the recommended answer, and ? followed by what
you do not understand marks it unclear. The answers are saved to the document.
A decision still unanswered or unclear exits 65 and is listed; an unclear one
names roadmap questions to rewrite it. The answered document is snapshotted to
the roadmap run's decisions.md. Every task run copies it and names it in each
turn manifest as ROADMAP_DECISIONS, binding human direction for Planner,
Builder, and Reviewer.

The roadmap run stops at the first task run that stops, with its exit code (20,
21, or 22), and never answers a stop, approves a gate, skips a task, or merges.
Its stop block adds 'forgecycle: stop: roadmap_run=… kind=task_run_stopped …'
and 'forgecycle: next: forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>': recover the
task run with task commands, then resume the roadmap run. A child that creates
no task run exits with its own code (task_run_start_failed). An integration
branch checked out in a worktree stops it with exit 21; a moved integration
branch or a head that is not a fast-forward fails it with exit 22.

When every task is done, it writes result.md and prints 'git merge --ff-only
forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id>' as the human decision that integrates it.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops the running child task command, which records its task
run's stop as task run does; the roadmap run passes SIGTERM on when only it got
the signal. It then starts or resumes no other task run and prints 'forgecycle:
next: forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>'.

forgecycle pause, from another terminal, stops the roadmap run once its task
run's current turn ends, or before it starts the next task run, with the stop
kind pause_requested and exit 21; forgecycle unpause continues it.

See also: forgecycle help roadmap status, forgecycle help roadmap resume
```

## forgecycle roadmap status

Show a roadmap run's tasks, its stop, and what to do next.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap status [--json] <roadmap-run-id>

Show a roadmap run's tasks, its stop, and what to do next.

Arguments:
  <roadmap-run-id>  A roadmap run ID, as roadmap run prints it and status lists
                    it

Options:
  --json            Print the stored state document
                    (schemas/roadmap-run-state.schema.json)
  -h, --help        Show this help

roadmap status prints the state (a running roadmap run with no live process is
reported as interrupted), the manifest, the base, the integration branch and
head, and each task's status, latest task run, attempt, and integrated head. A
stopped roadmap run also shows its stop kind, reason, and Next lines; a done
one shows its result.md and the merge line.

See also: forgecycle help status
```

## forgecycle roadmap resume

Continue a stopped, failed, or interrupted roadmap run.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap resume [options] <roadmap-run-id>

Continue a stopped, failed, or interrupted roadmap run.

Arguments:
  <roadmap-run-id>  A roadmap run ID, as roadmap run prints it and status lists
                    it

Options:
  --planner ID      Use candidate ID as Planner for the task runs this
                    invocation starts or resumes
  --builder ID      Use candidate ID as Builder for the task runs this
                    invocation starts or resumes; not a read-only candidate
  --reviewer ID     Use candidate ID as Reviewer for the task runs this
                    invocation starts or resumes
  --auto-resume     Turn automatic resume on for the rest of the roadmap run
  -h, --help        Show this help

roadmap resume looks at the current task's latest task run:
  - done: it is integrated and the next task starts
  - abandoned: the task is retried with a new task run (the next attempt) on
    the unchanged integration head
  - interrupted, or paused on request (pause_requested): it is continued with
    forgecycle task resume
  - stopped otherwise (paused, blocked, failed, or awaiting approval): its stop
    block and exit code are reported and nothing else happens; recover it first
    with task resume, task approve, task reject, or task abandon

It refuses with exit 21 while another process advances the roadmap run or the
task run.

See also: forgecycle help roadmap status
```

## forgecycle roadmap abandon

Stop a roadmap run; keep its integration branch and task runs.

```text
Usage: forgecycle roadmap abandon <roadmap-run-id>

Stop a roadmap run; keep its integration branch and task runs.

Arguments:
  <roadmap-run-id>  A roadmap run ID, as roadmap run prints it and status lists
                    it

Options:
  -h, --help        Show this help

Only the roadmap run is abandoned. A stopped task run keeps the repository
reservation until forgecycle task abandon releases it.

To skip a stuck task, abandon the roadmap run and start a new one on its
integration branch:
  forgecycle roadmap run <manifest> \
    --base forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id> \
    --skip <done IDs>,<stuck ID>
```
